title: CRM and ERP Development in South Carolina
metaTitle: CRM and ERP Development in South Carolina | TDM
metaDescription: Custom CRM and ERP systems for South Carolina manufacturers, suppliers, logistics firms and service businesses: sales, inventory, finance and operations in one place.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) builds custom CRM and ERP systems for South Carolina businesses: a CRM shaped around how your team sells, and ERP modules for inventory, purchasing, HR, finance and operations. Much of the state's economy makes, moves or stores physical goods, from Upstate suppliers to warehouses near the Port of Charleston, and that is the kind of company that outgrows spreadsheets first.

sections.heading: Why South Carolina companies outgrow spreadsheets
paragraphs: The Upstate is built around manufacturing. BMW assembles vehicles in Spartanburg County, Michelin runs its North American business from Greenville, and around them sit many smaller suppliers of parts, tooling, plastics, packaging and services. A supplier in that chain lives on delivery dates, lot traceability and accurate stock. When quotes sit in one file, orders in another and inventory in a third, the mistakes show up as late shipments.

The Lowcountry has a similar pattern with different goods. Boeing builds aircraft in North Charleston, Volvo builds cars in Berkeley County, and the port feeds warehouses, freight forwarders and trucking firms along I-26 and up to the inland port at Greer. These companies track containers, appointments, storage and billing, often across more than one site.

Then there are the businesses that sell time rather than goods: contractors, medical practices, property managers on the coast, staffing firms. Their problem is usually the customer record. Leads arrive by phone, web form and referral, and nobody can see which ones were followed up.

sections.heading: What a custom system covers
paragraphs: Off-the-shelf software charges per seat and expects you to work its way. A custom system models your own pipeline stages, approval steps, stock locations and reporting lines. We build only the modules you need now, on an architecture that lets the next one slot in later.
bullets: CRM: lead capture, pipeline stages, contact histories, task automation and follow-up workflows.
Inventory and warehouse: stock by location, purchasing, receiving and movements between sites.
Finance: invoicing and expenses, connected to the accounting software you already use.
HR: attendance and payroll records for shift-based and multi-site teams.
Dashboards by role, so a plant manager, a sales lead and an owner each see their own numbers.
Role-based access, so staff see only what their job requires.

sections.heading: Connecting to what you already run
paragraphs: Few South Carolina companies start from nothing. There is usually an accounting package, a website with a quote form, perhaps an online store, and a customer portal that a large buyer requires you to use. A new system is only useful if it talks to those. We build two-way integrations with your website, store, accounting tools, email, payment gateways and logistics providers so that nobody types the same order twice.

Moving off old software is the risky part. We migrate historical data in a structured way: mapped, cleaned, deduplicated and checked against the source before the old system is retired. For a supplier with years of part numbers and customer pricing, that check matters more than any new feature.

sections.heading: What to check before you commission one
paragraphs: Ask who will own the code and the data when the project ends. Ask how the system will be hosted and backed up, and what happens during a hurricane evacuation on the coast if your office is closed for a week. Ask to start with one module and prove it before funding the rest. If your customers impose quality or traceability requirements, or if you handle patient or student records, raise that in the first conversation so the requirements shape the design rather than being added afterwards.

faqs.q: Do you build CRM and ERP software for South Carolina manufacturers?
faqs.a: Yes. We build custom CRM and ERP modules for manufacturers and suppliers, covering sales, inventory, purchasing, finance and operations. We start from how your plant and office actually work, then build the modules you need first.

faqs.q: Is a custom ERP better than buying an existing product?
faqs.a: Not always. If a standard product fits your process, buy it. Custom makes sense when your workflow is unusual, when per-seat fees keep growing as you hire, or when you are stitching several tools together by hand. We will tell you which case you are in.

faqs.q: How much does a custom CRM or ERP cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the number of modules, the integrations and the amount of data to migrate. We quote after a free consultation, once we understand your process and what is already in place.

faqs.q: How long does it take to build?
faqs.a: It depends on your requirements and the brief. A single module is a very different project from a full system. The timeline is agreed in the project plan before work starts, and modules are released one at a time.

faqs.q: Can you connect the system to our accounting software and website?
faqs.a: Yes. Integrations with your website, online store, accounting tools, email, payment gateways and logistics providers are a standard part of the work, so data is entered once and flows where it is needed.
